text:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden spike of 503s for hosted-infer-prod (us-west-2) on /v1/generate — 78 errors/min, p95 latency 3.2s :rotating_light:

support-alex: Customer Jason (acct jason-inc) called in. They see intermittent 503s and timeouts since ~03:05 UTC. Repro steps: hitting bulk generate (concurrent 40 reqs, max_tokens=1024) — ~20% fail with 503, rest succeed but slow. They pasted one curl response:

    $ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"model":"redwood-large-13b","input":"hello"}'
    HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
    content-type: application/json
    {"error":"upstream inference worker crashed while handling request"}

support-alex: Attached customer logs show container restart events and a single segfault in the worker process. Adding SRE and runtime. @sre-lin @eng-runtime-anya

sre-lin: I'm seeing the same in infra metrics — GPU node group gpu-hosts-usw2 scaled normally but kubelet shows repeated PodOOM or OOMKills on infer-runner on nodes 04 and 08. dmesg on node-04 contains:

    [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:04:00) 79: Xid (CLUSTER) 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
    [ 12345.679000] kernel: gpu 0000:04:00.0: fatal error, reporting and recovering
    [ 12345.679100] infer-runner[2231]: segfault (signal 11)

sre-lin: Also seeing repeated kernel Oops lines referencing ttm/vm and dma mapping failures — looks like a kernel-level page fault after a cudaMalloc failing with ENOMEM despite free memory reported. Possibly memory fragmentation after recent allocator changes.

eng-runtime-anya: We pushed the dynamic-batch-allocator v2 last night (03:02 UTC) to improve memory packing. It changed allocation pooling for KV cache and temp tensors. Rolling that back now on a small canary. Early hypothesis: fragmentation under high-concurrency long-context workloads is causing cudaMalloc to return ENOMEM which triggers a path that can dereference freed memory, leading to SIGSEGV.

infra-oz: Node 08 shows repeated container restarts; kubelet event snippet:

    Normal  Killing    2m (x5 over 12m)  kubelet  Killing container with id docker://infer-runner:container killed due to SIGKILL

    Warning OOMKilled    30s (x7 over 10m)  kubelet  Pod was OOMKilled

support-manager-maya: Customer impact: jason-inc has ~1500 requests/min, saw 20% error rate for ~10 minutes, some inflight requests hit 500/503 and timed out. They've escalated to priority. We promised updates every 15m.

eng-runtime-anya: Immediate mitigations I'm applying now:
- revert dynamic-batch-allocator v2 on hosted-infer-prod canary group (rolling restart of canary pods)
- add a temporary gating config to refuse large concurrent requests (>20) for redwood-large-13b routes in us-west-2
- enable fallback routing to redwood-medium-6b for 10% of traffic from the affected customer

sre-lin: Operational steps I'm doing in parallel:
- cordon and drain node-08 (gpus) to avoid repeated restarts: `kubectl drain node-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- capture full dmesg and nvml logs: `sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.node-08.log` and `nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-state.node-08.xml`
- pull the most recent infer-runner logs: `kubectl logs -n hosted-infer infer-runner-abc -c infer-runner --previous > /tmp/infer-runner.prev.log`

eng-runtime-anya: Also instructing team to gather a gdb backtrace if the process still coredumps: `gcore $(pgrep infer-runner)` then `gdb /usr/local/bin/infer-runner core.<pid> -ex 'bt full' -ex quit` and upload to s3://redwood-incidents/2055551234/

support-alex: Running a quick repro locally with a stress harness (concurrent 50, seq_len 4096) — I can reproduce one crash after ~120s on a similar config. Pasting the worker stderr around crash:

    E 03:07:52.123 infer-runner: [memory] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2) at src/alloc.c:412
    W 03:07:52.124 infer-runner: attempting fallback allocation path
    E 03:07:52.125 infer-runner: invalid read after free at src/kv_cache.c:233
    F 03:07:52.126 infer-runner: segfault: signal 11

infra-oz: For a fast customer-facing mitigation, we can throttle concurrent requests per-API-key in the gateway for affected endpoints and region. I can push a rule to limit to 15 concurrent requests per key for /v1/generate in us-west-2. That should reduce pressure immediately.

support-manager-maya: Please do throttle now and notify customer. Alex, offer them temporary reduced concurrency and fallback route while we investigate.

eng-runtime-anya: We'll keep the canary rollback running. If that prevents repro on canary, we'll escalate to a full rollback. We're also adding extra null-checks and guardrails in the allocator path; a patch will be ready for review in 45m.

sre-lin: Next steps and owners:
- infra-oz: throttle per-key concurrency in gateway (now) — ONGOING
- eng-runtime-anya: rollback dynamic-batch-allocator canary and prepare hotfix (10-45m) — ONGOING
- sre-lin: collect node coredumps / nvml / dmesg and add to incident bucket (15m) — ONGOING
- support-alex: update customer every 15m, offer workaround (fallback route + throttling) — ONGOING

customer.jason: Thanks for the quick response. We'll accept the fallback to medium model for now. Please keep us posted.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2055551234 — Severity: P2 (customer impacting). Pager duty notified for infra and runtime teams.

support-alex: Updating customer: we've applied throttling to reduce bursts, routed 10% to a smaller model, and rolled back the canary on a subset. Engineers are collecting coredumps. Next update in 15m. :thumbsup:
